questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture, possibility of nature experiences, language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If I had received on-campus accommodation, it would have been a 10

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study abroad and the Erasmus+ coordinators were great at reaching out to the students. It made it easy to know who to contact in case it was needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. I would recommend waiting to apply for exchange in Ireland until the housing crisis is not as bad as it currently is.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The living standards are not as high as we are used to in Denmark. And it is pretty expensive. I paid the same to live in inner Copenhagen as I paid to live 7,5 km from the university/10 km from the city centre.
Start your accommodation search early - maybe even before knowing whether you receive on-campus accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The people who had on-campus accommodation had a nice living situation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We received a mail that took us through it step-by-step. I do not remember the exact process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The academic team at the host institution.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. We had the first week to try out the classes we were interested in and then we chose.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It will all work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mostly 4th year classes and a 2nd year course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller classes and more contact with your teacher - very nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Comparative European Politics, 
Policy-making in the European Union,
Russian Politics,
Sociology of gender and popular culture, 
Nationalism, ethnicity and conflict

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Russian Politics, Sociology of gender and popular culture, Nationalism, ethnicity and conflict. They were interesting and had a  nice work load.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was not as expensive. However, I spend a lot more on food and personal stuff (mainly to travel around and see the country) than I normally do as I wanted to experience as much as possible

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have so many nice clubs and societies - try them out!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds - something for everybody

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Kayaking! So fun and a great club with great people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the nature, it is breathtaking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the Irish people are not very different from the Danish people except they are more warm and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: We as Danish students are often older than the Irish students and students from other countries (the only country where the students seemed to be the same age as me (23) were from the Netherlands).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and willingness to help

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go out and experience the country - do not stay at the campus or in Limerick the entire time.
Be prepared for rain. It is not a problem if you buy some nice gear for rainy days.
Take the housing crisis into consideration when applying. I would not have done anything differently but my housing situation did have a significantly negative impact on my stay. However, I think that around 75% were offered on-campus accommodation so I was just pretty unlucky.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out to the receiving institution if you have any problems, they are very helpful

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing the nature side with my new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My housing situation. I had to bike to the university as public transportation does not function very well in Ireland and the roads were dark, narrow and had a speed limit of 80 km/h. Moreover, my accommodation was overpriced when considering that there was mould in my room, my room was impossible to heat up, the oven did not work and I shared one kitchen and one bathroom with three to five people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
